question: Where can I get a list of commercial ports in the United States, with location, port authority and annual cargo, passengers and vessel calls?

answer.summary: USACE's 'port' is a statistical area with a numeric code: its Principal Ports layer gives CY2023 short tons for the top 150 (2.6 billion short tons) and its Port layer gives 370 port polygons with legal descriptions. BTS Port Data adds TEU, tonnage and vessel calls (48 ports, 2023) by the same code; cruise passengers exist for the top 25. USACE Navigation Facilities lists 9,491 docks with owner and operator text. No port-authority field exists; names mix ports and authorities.
main_caveats: A USACE port is a statistical area with a code (Houston 2031, Long Beach 4110, New York & New Jersey 398), not an authority or terminal. Names differ by file: Houston Port Authority, TX vs Port of Houston Authority of Harris County, TX.
USACE tonnage is in short tons for CY2023 and covers 150 ports ranked by total tonnage. BTS Port Data uses TEU for containers and short tons for bulk; Top 25 TEU tables carry no year.
TEU and ranks differ between BTS tables: Long Beach 2023 is 4,786,383 TEU in Port Data but 6,091,978 TEU (imports plus exports plus domestic) in the undated Top 25 table; not reconciled.
Vessel calls in BTS Port Data are fractional (Long Beach container 656.5) and exist for 48 ports; cruise passengers cover the top 25 cruise ports only.
Docks have 20,574 features, only 9,491 of type Dock; 3,144 docks have operator text and 6,870 owner text; several Long Beach berths share one coordinate.
usace.army.mil, bts.gov and maritime.dot.gov pages refused default curl requests (403); the ArcGIS services and data.bts.gov tables were reachable.
answer.confidence_reason: USACE layers and BTS tables were queried and cross-checked for Houston and Long Beach, but WCSC, MARAD and authority sources were unreachable or unread and several definitions stay unreconciled.

attributes.note: Port polygons: 150 principal ports (CY2023) and 370 port areas with legal descriptions; terminals as points in Navigation Facilities (20,574 features, 9,491 docks).
No authority field. Port-area names often carry it (Authority 56, District 44, Commission 10 of 370); descriptions cite the law; dock OWNERS gives terminal owners.
attributes.gap_note: MARAD's port authority list (403 to curl) and AAPA's 2026 member directory (a viewer) were not read. Names differ between files: Houston Port Authority vs Port of Houston Authority of Harris County.

attributes.note: CY2023 short tons for 150 principal ports; BTS Port Data gives total, dry bulk and container TEU by port and year 2016-2023; Top 25 tables lack a stated year.
attributes.gap_note: Tonnage for the other 220 port areas and the WCSC annual tables were not opened: USACE WCSC pages returned 403 to curl and ndclibrary did not connect.

attributes.note: Cruise passenger arrivals for the top 25 ports in 2023 (Miami 3,809,753) and a national series 2019-2023; no ferry or other passenger counts were found.
attributes.gap_note: Ferry and other passenger counts per port were not found in the files tested; USACE WCSC passenger tables and port authority reports were not opened.

attributes.note: BTS Port Data gives vessel calls by vessel type for 48 ports per year 2020-2023 (Long Beach 2023: 2,263 across five types, with fractional values).
attributes.gap_note: Only 48 ports are covered. MARAD vessel call data (page 403 to curl) and port authority statistics were not opened.

sources.name: Principal Ports (USACE, distributed in NTAD)
sources.publisher: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Waterborne Commerce Statistics Center; distributed by BTS in NTAD
sources.format: ArcGIS REST FeatureServer (polygons, JSON); a geo.dot.gov copy exists at /hosted/principal_ports_view/FeatureServer/0
sources.license: CC0 1.0 (data.gov record); the same record flags the access level as non-public
sources.summary: USACE CY2023 tonnage for the 150 principal ports (short tons) with port polygons and USACE port codes.
sources.coverage_note: Top 150 ports only; a port is a USACE statistical area, not an authority.
caveats: Short tons; ports ranked by total tonnage.
Names differ from the Port layer for 64 codes.

problems: The TYPE value Internal differs from the dictionary value Inland.
The data.gov record marks the access level as non-public while giving a CC0 license.

example.example_result: Rank 1: PORT 2031, Coastal, Houston Port Authority, TX, TOTAL 309531236, DOMESTIC 80511805, FOREIGN_ 229019431, IMPORTS 61307109, EXPORTS 167712322; rank 4 New York, NY & NJ 132289509; rank 6 Port of Long Beach, CA 85260786.

sources.name: Port Data (BTS Port Performance Freight Statistics Program)
sources.summary: BTS table with container TEU, dry bulk and total tonnage and vessel calls by port and year (2016-2023) keyed by USACE port code.
sources.coverage_note: 55 port codes over time; vessel calls only for 48 ports (2020-2023).
caveats: Use trade_type TOTAL, not a sum of all types.

problems: The old data.transportation.gov resource URL redirects (302) to data.bts.gov.
bts.gov/ports and the 2026 annual report pages returned 403 to curl.

example.example_result: Long Beach, CA Port of 2023: TOTAL TONNAGE 85260786 short tons (rank 6); CONTAINER TOTAL 4786383 TEUs (rank 3); VESSEL CALLS Container 656.5, Other Freight 877, Other Freight Barge 357, Dry Bulk 238, Dry Bulk Barge 134.5.

sources.name: Port and Port Statistical Area (Port Areas, USACE, distributed in NTAD)
sources.publisher: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Waterborne Commerce Statistics Center; distributed by BTS in NTAD
sources.format: ArcGIS REST FeatureServer (layer 0 Ports, layer 1 PortStatisticalAreas; JSON)
sources.license: Unknown (data.gov record shows no license text read)
sources.summary: USACE boundaries and legal descriptions for 370 US ports and 7 statistical areas, keyed by the port code used in USACE and BTS tables.
sources.coverage_note: Boundaries only; no authority field and no activity figures.
caveats: A port is a statistical boundary, not an authority.
Names differ from Principal Ports for 64 codes.

problems: The geodata.bts.gov dataset page and the guessed NTAD service URLs were not usable; the service came from the DOI redirect.

example.example_result: PORTIDPK 2031: Port of Houston Authority of Harris County, TX, DATA_YEAR 2019, territory as described by the Texas Special District Local Laws Code; PORTIDPK 4110: Port of Long Beach, CA, DATA_YEAR 2020, defined by the City of Long Beach charter section 229t.

sources.name: Navigation Facilities (Docks) (USACE, distributed in NTAD)
sources.publisher: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Waterborne Commerce Statistics Center; distributed by BTS in NTAD
sources.license: Unknown (layer copyright: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers)
sources.summary: USACE docks and terminals: 9,491 Dock features with port code, coordinates and free-text owner and operator.
sources.coverage_note: Owner and operator text present on 6,870 and 3,144 docks; several berths share one coordinate.

problems: The service uses FAC_TYPE and PSA_NAME where the dictionary names FACILITY_TYPE and PSA.

example.example_result: First feature: PORT OF LONG BEACH, PIER T BERTHS 132-140, FAC_TYPE Dock, PORT 4110, OPERATORS 'Current Operator: Hanjin Container Line Phone: 562-256-2600', LATITUDE 33.75097, LONGITUDE -118.21395, SERVICE_INITIATION_DATE 01-JAN-1990. Long Beach has 73 Dock features.

sources.license: Public domain (Socrata licenseId PUBLIC_DOMAIN where stated)

bts.gov report pages returned 403 to curl, so the year was not confirmed.

example.example_result: 25 rows; first: Port Authority of New York and New Jersey, NY & NJ, Foreign Imports 5,352,134, Foreign Exports 1,252,065, Domestic 56,118; Port of Long Beach, CA 4,675,674, 1,056,910, 359,394. Cruise 2023: Miami, FL 3,809,753 passengers.

members_summary.scope_note: Universe: BTS port tables found by catalog search on data.bts.gov (about 18 hits for port performance, tonnage and vessel calls). Tested: Top 25 TEU (downloaded) and the two cruise tables (queried); dry bulk and monthly TEU were read as metadata only; others (dwell times, air drafts, import commodities) are out of scope.

local_terms.term: Principal Ports of the United States
local_terms.meaning: USACE list of the 150 ports with the highest tonnage, published in NTAD as Principal Ports.
BTS program whose tables (Port Data, Top 25) sit on data.bts.gov.
USACE reporting area that groups ports for commerce statistics.
USACE terminal and dock list with owners and operators.
Waterborne Commerce Statistics Center and the Waterborne Commerce of the United States reports.
Unit of USACE and BTS tonnage figures.
Twenty-foot equivalent units, the container count unit.
United Nations location code carried by Navigation Facilities.
